title: OpenAI Responses behavioral delta catalog and runtime fallback policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: As we provide a compatibility surface for the OpenAI Responses API, there are subtle behavioral deltas that affect customer integrations across streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. These differences cause downstream SDKs and customer code to see spurious errors, inconsistent event ordering, and non-deterministic parser failures.

Scope: Catalog observed behavioral differences, define a prioritized runtime fallback policy that preserves application semantics, and produce a test matrix plus canary plan. This ticket focuses on behavioral deltas (not performance tuning or kernel-level changes).

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Produce a concise delta catalog with examples that reproduce failures in our test harness.
- Define a runtime fallback policy that decides when to 1) translate, 2) emulate, or 3) surface the upstream behavior to customers. Policy must include ordering for streaming events, tool-call handoff, and structured-output mismatch resolution.
- Implement small runtime shim hooks for three prioritized deltas (stream chunk boundaries, late tool call resolution, structured JSON partial emission) behind a feature flag.
- Add automated integration tests per the test matrix and run a canary against dedicated staging with synthetic workloads.
- Update docs (Console and API reference) describing behavioral guarantees and known mismatch list.

Out of scope: full performance re-architecture, alternate kernel selection, or changes to public SDKs outside our compatibility shim.

Key stakeholders: runtime, api, sdks, docs, support.

Deliverables:
- Delta catalog (this ticket's artifacts)
- Feature-flagged runtime shim for targeted deltas
- Integration test suite and canary report
- Docs page and postmortem checklist for regressions
observed_deltas: Streaming chunk granularity: OpenAI Responses emits SSE-style events with partial tokens in some models; our runtime historically emits token-aligned chunks leading to differences in client buffering behavior.

Event ordering on tool-calls: Responses API can emit tool_call event then text chunks that reference the call; our current tool routing assumes completion-of-stream before tool handoff, causing lost context in edge cases.

Function argument typing: Responses sometimes serialize function arguments with top-level numbers/booleans (no quotes) while our structured-output validator expects quoted strings for legacy parity checks.
Partial JSON emission: Some responses emit incremental JSON that is invalid until the final chunk; our structured-output guard rejects intermediate chunks and terminates the stream early.
Error semantics on ambiguous function resolution: Responses surfaces a 200 with tool_call intent but missing 'name' field; our parser treats this as a protocol error and returns 500 to the customer.
Connection close behavior: Upstream occasionally closes the connection after final SSE without an explicit 'done' event; clients relying on the event are impacted.
Idempotency token handling: Responses allows duplicate idempotency tokens across near-simultaneous requests; our dedupe layer discards legitimate parallel calls for some SDK patterns.
priority_rationale: High frequency surfaces in customer-reported integrations (support tickets).
Can cause data loss or unexpected 'internal error' surface to customers when tool-calls are misrouted.
Fixes are amenable to localized runtime shims and operators can toggle via feature flags for safe rollout.
runtime_fallback_policy: Step 1: Attempt translation layer that maps upstream event types to our canonical event model with minimal mutation (safe, idempotent mappings).

Step 2: For streaming partial JSON, buffer until a configurable soft-threshold (e.g., 2s or 8KB) and attempt incremental parse; if buffer exceeds threshold, fall back to best-effort string emission and flag in trace.
Step 3: For ambiguous tool_call events missing 'name', synthesize a placeholder name and route to a quarantined tool-runner that returns a structured tool-error to caller instead of 500.
Step 4: If translation fails or introduces >5% regression in latency observed on canary, surface upstream raw events under a 'raw_responses' opt-in header and mark as 'legacy-mode' in logs.
test_matrix: Streaming: SSE vs chunked transfer reproduction across sequence lengths, with client reassembly assertions and end-of-stream semantics.

Tool-calling: simulate tool_call emitted before, during, and after text tokens and validate that arguments, name, and handoff ordering result in consistent tool invocation or well-defined error payloads.
Structured-output: incremental JSON emission cases, invalid intermediate chunks, and numeric/boolean typing differences validated against SDK parsers.
Retry and idempotency: concurrent requests with identical idempotency tokens and with network flaps to validate dedupe logic.
Connection semantics: abrupt close, graceful done event, and long-poll keepalive scenarios.
implementation_notes: Implement translation hooks in runtime::responses_compat module behind 'resp_compat_v1' feature flag.
Provide tracing tags: compat.delta_id, compat.action, compat.synthesized_name for observability and post-canary analysis.
Add metrics: compat.translate.success, compat.translate.failure, compat.buffer.exceeded, compat.synthetic_tool_runs.
Keep shims small and reversible; wire feature flag to Console rollout controls for safe on/off per customer.
canary_plan: Phase A: Internal staging with synthetic workloads covering top 10 delta cases (2d).
Phase B: 5% production traffic diverted to compat shim with strict obs and auto rollback on error spike (3d).
Phase C: Expand to 25% with monitoring of customer error rates, latency P50/P95, and SDK parser exceptions (5d).
Rollback criteria: >2x customer-visible errors, >15% regression in P95 latency, or increased tool-run failures.
docs_and_communication: Publish a compatibility note in API reference describing supported and unsupported behaviors and the 'raw_responses' opt-in.
Notify SDK teams with changelog entry and test vectors for parser teams to validate.
Create a runbook for support with reproduction steps and mitigation toggles.
